clue.text: Very short of time at start of long year

indicators.note: the time letter is placed at the front of the rest

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Someone running out of time at the beginning of a long year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at start of' puts T before ITCH and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Titchy is informal British slang for tiny, very small or very short.

clue.text: Person working hard, not prepared to get upset in protracted conflict

parts.note: to work like a Trojan is to work very hard

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read the word bottom to top

parts.note: raw means unprepared, uncooked

explanation.surface: A hard worker, not ready for it, getting upset in a long-running dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get upset' turns RAW into WAR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan War of Greek legend lasted ten years, a famously long conflict.

clue.text: It's said to convey sympathy on that issue

definitions.meaning: a word of comfort, usually said twice to someone upset
in that respect, on that point

explanation.surface: Someone offers sympathy on a sensitive subject.
explanation.definitionFit: 'There, there' soothes the upset, and the same word means in that respect: 'there I disagree'.

clue.text: What's set up by Record Bureau providing support to customers?

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so the exclamation reads backwards

parts.note: eh is a questioning exclamation like what
an LP is a long-playing record
a bureau is a writing desk

explanation.surface: A record office asking what has been set up to support customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns EH into HE in this down clue; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A help desk is a service that gives assistance to customers or users.

clue.text: I stop you moving cows in India, say

indicators.note: the cattle word sits inside the continent word, as the clue says cows in India

parts.note: India is an example of a country in Asia
kine is an old plural of cow

explanation.surface: In India the sacred cows are allowed to block traffic and stop you moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks India as only an example of the continent, and 'in' is the container signal; the definition is the condition speaking in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: Akinesia is the medical term for loss or impairment of voluntary movement, so the condition itself might say it stops you moving.

clue.text: Refuse to locate this prehistoric site, kind cement hid after rebuilding

definitions.text: Refuse to locate this prehistoric site

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Builders hid cement of a kind in the course of rebuilding an ancient site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the noun, rubbish, not the verb; prehistoric rubbish heaps help archaeologists find settlements.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen midden is a prehistoric refuse heap of shells and bones that marks an ancient dwelling site.

clue.text: Foreigner in Alpine resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sorting again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A foreign visitor at a ski resort in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but reads as re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nepali is a person from Nepal, and so a foreigner to a British setter.

clue.text: Plain is dry, note — obtain start of irrigation

parts.note: sere means dry, withered
to get is to obtain

indicators.note: the first letter of the word irrigation

explanation.surface: A dry plain needs irrigation to get started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' gives I from irrigation; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast grassland plain in Tanzania.

clue.text: Correspond with a person abroad, dispatching letter finally

indicators.note: the person word sends off its final letter

parts.note: a Greek is a person from abroad, a foreigner

explanation.surface: Writing to a foreign pen friend and sending off the last letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatching letter finally' removes K from GREEK.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that correspond agree or match each other.

clue.text: Common area of interest ended by China withdrawing

parts.note: something ended is over

indicators.note: the word for a friend is drawn back, read from right to left

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal

explanation.surface: A shared sphere of interest ended when China pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: China = PAL comes from Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' = mate; 'withdrawing' turns PAL into LAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Where two fields overlap they share a common region, the part both cover.

clue.text: Form of respiratory covering that is a hangover cure?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters cover, that is go round, the abbreviation
a form of a word is a version of it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A kind of breathing mask that doubles as a cure for a hangover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' shuffles the respiratory letters, and 'covering' means those shuffled letters go round the abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie oyster is a raw egg with Worcestershire sauce and seasoning, swallowed whole as a hangover remedy.

clue.text: Maker of video that's entertaining about one having a spill

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so the word for about sits inside the maker

parts.note: someone who tapes a programme is a taper
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A video maker who has been entertaining someone with a mishap or fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' is the container signal. A spill is a thin strip of wood or paper for lighting, not a fall, so 'having a spill' means carrying one.
explanation.definitionFit: A taperer is one who carries a taper, and a spill is a thin taper for lighting candles or pipes.

clue.text: A hallucinogenic drug-taker giving up

parts.note: a head is slang for a habitual drug user, as in acid head

explanation.surface: An LSD user deciding to quit the habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' is a link word; 'up' is the definition, as in being two goals up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up in a contest means leading, in front of your opponent.

clue.text: Description of shock nobles had after revolution?

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: How aristocrats felt when the revolution came and swept them away.
explanation.walkthrough: A shock here is a thick mass of hair, not a fright; the anagram of NOBLESHAD gives a pale hair colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair can be described by its colour, and a pale greyish-blonde is one such shade.

clue.text: Plentiful supply of quiet sort of road at cathedral town

indicators.note: the quiet road pieces stand at the cathedral town, following it

parts.note: Wells is a small cathedral city in Somerset, England
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a ring road circles a town

explanation.surface: A quiet ring road near a cathedral town provides plenty of something.
explanation.walkthrough: WELLS is an English cathedral city in Somerset; 'at' sets P and RING beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellspring is a source, so figuratively an abundant, continual supply.

clue.text: Forgotten reason for write-off

parts.note: something forgotten is lost to memory
a cause is a reason

explanation.surface: Someone forgot why a debt was written off.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is a hopeless case, something to be written off as a failure.

clue.text: Nonentity — ending as nothing too

definitions.meaning: in grammar a null or empty inflection, as in the plural of sheep

explanation.surface: A nobody whose story finishes with nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions joined by 'as' and 'too': the grammarian's null inflection is the middle one.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is informally called a cipher or nought, a null inflection has the same name, and the number nought is its plain sense.

clue.text: Religious work written by woman's full of insight and different

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a religious work
her is the possessive for a woman
wise means full of insight

explanation.surface: A woman's religious book, insightful and unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written by' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise can mean in a different way or different, as in 'he could not be otherwise'.

clue.text: No favouritism being shown in English class

parts.note: quality, as in a player of class, means high standard

explanation.surface: A fair-minded teacher in an English lesson shows no favourites.
explanation.definitionFit: Equality is the state of all being treated alike, with nobody favoured.

clue.text: Race attack

definitions.meaning: to race is to hurry along at speed
to charge at someone, as in American football or a sudden assault

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the word: hurrying headlong, and charging at an opponent.

clue.text: Drop half of late investigations when in pickle

indicators.note: the half word goes inside the pickle word

parts.note: a relish is a pickle or chutney

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for investigations is kept

parts.note: inquests are investigations into the deaths of the late

explanation.surface: Abandoning half the inquiries into a recent death when in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, so the investigations are the inquiries held into deaths; 'half of' keeps the front half and 'in' sets it inside the pickle. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To relinquish something is to give it up or let it go, to drop it.

clue.text: Backers of crooks shifting ecstasy up north

indicators.note: a letter in the word is moved to a new place
in a down clue going north means moving toward the top of the word

parts.note: a crook is a bend, an angle
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Gangsters' financiers moving drugs to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' and 'up north' move E higher in ANGLES in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Angels are financial backers, especially of a theatre production.

clue.text: Slash requirement to import ultimate in trendy stock

parts.note: to hack is to cut or slash

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so the letter goes inside the requirement word

parts.note: a need is a requirement

indicators.note: the final letter of the word trendy

explanation.surface: Cutting the import requirement on fashionable goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate in' gives Y from trendy, which 'to import' puts inside NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock phrase is a trite, overused one, the same idea as hackneyed.

clue.text: Get lost following dance hits endlessly

indicators.note: the trimmed word comes after the dance word

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance

indicators.note: the word hits loses its letters at both ends

explanation.surface: Leave the dance, which keeps playing hits without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips the first and last letters from hits, and 'following' puts what is left after the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hop it is British slang telling someone to go away, like 'get lost'.

clue.text: Emotion at centre of Austen novel?

indicators.note: only the middle part of the novel's title is kept

parts.note: Northanger Abbey is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: Asking which feeling lies at the heart of a Jane Austen book.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of NORTHANGER ABBEY, with NORTH and ABBEY removed, is the emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is a strong feeling of displeasure, one of the basic emotions.

clue.text: Converse of bad egg's approving expression

parts.note: the opposite of bad is good
O looks like an egg

explanation.surface: The opposite of a bad egg is someone to approve of.
explanation.walkthrough: A bad egg is a rogue; its converse, 'good egg', gives GOOD + O.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-o is a dated British exclamation of approval, like 'jolly good'.

clue.text: Discreet page at front of dirty book collection

indicators.note: the page letter is placed before the rest

parts.note: rude means smutty, dirty
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A careful page boy at the front of a smutty anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at front of' places the page letter first; the book collection is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudent and discreet both describe someone cautious and careful in judgement.

clue.text: New impression made by witchcraft in African capital

parts.note: an air is an impression or appearance someone gives
obi or obeah is a form of West Indian sorcery

explanation.surface: A fresh image created by magic in a city in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: OBI is a crossword staple: Caribbean witchcraft, also spelt obeah.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Bank of river feeding into estuary resort

indicators.note: the river letter goes into the shuffled letters
to re-sort is to sort again, rearranging these letters

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The bank of a river flowing into a seaside resort at its estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' is read as re-sort, the anagram signal, turning ESTUARY into TEASURY; 'feeding into' places R after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasury is a store of money, the same function as a bank.

clue.text: Holy cow upset Indian city

parts.note: holy cow and my are both exclamations of surprise
sore means upset or aggrieved

explanation.surface: A sacred cow is distressed in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy cow' looks like India's sacred cattle but is just an exclamation, as is 'my!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysore is a city in Karnataka, southern India.
